fieldNotes.location: Roster coords pointed at downtown Sweetwater (4 km off). Actual GP Gypsum complex is on FM 1856 off I-20 east of Sweetwater (310/311 FM 1856): the legacy plant (Nolan County since 1957) plus the new $325M plant opened Oct 2023. Confirmed by GP-branded blue perimeter fencing in Street View; locked center ~32.4830,-100.3345.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Plant reached via FM 1856, a county road dead-ending into the GP complex; GP-logo privacy-screened perimeter fence confirmed in Street View. Controlled-access industrial site with a clear entrance driveway and flags. No public-road pass-through.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No staffed booth crisply resolved; modern GP plants typically use scale-house / kiosk check-in. Marked remoteGs true as the likelier read; both flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.scale: A truck scale is expected at a gypsum plant (inbound aggregate, outbound board); not crisply confirmed in imagery.
fieldNotes.dropArea: The new-plant truck yard shows dozens of trailers staged in marked rows north of the building — substantial drop/staging capacity.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: A regular rhythm of dock doors is visible along the new plant's N building face; estimated 10-25.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Raw gypsum received from the adjacent quarry/mine via internal haul roads (SW); finished wallboard ships by truck and rail from the N/E truck yard — separate operations.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Two distinct wallboard plants on one campus (legacy plant + 2023 plant) plus process and material-handling buildings.
fieldNotes.truckGateCount: Likely 2 — a main office entrance off FM 1856 plus a truck-yard entrance serving the new plant; counted as 2 with medium confidence.
fieldNotes.railServed: A new rail crossing and spur were installed on FM 1856 to serve the new plant; rail line confirmed in satellite imagery.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Rural Nolan County, TX — open ranchland along I-20 east of the small city of Sweetwater.
